title: iText commercial use requires a paid license; commercial terms moved to subscription
summary: iText 7 Community is AGPLv3-only: any closed-source or proprietary use — including shipping iText in a closed product, serving PDFs from a web app, or paid ASP services — requires a commercial license with source-code disclosure otherwise. Commercial licenses moved from perpetual to annual subscription effective 2020-04-02. Companies depending on com.itextpdf artifacts in proprietary software must hold a commercial agreement or migrate.

evidences.excerpt: iText employs a dual-license model: commercial and AGPL licenses. Free use only where you also distribute your software as free open source. As soon as you want to use iText in a closed source, proprietary environment, you have to pay for your use of iText.

From April 2020 onwards, changing the commercial model from perpetual license to annual subscription. Applies to all new customers and new installations from April 2nd, 2020; open-source AGPL and commercial licenses remain the dual scheme for companies that cannot comply with AGPL conditions.
